claims.claim: Mt Holland expansion creates a concrete multi-year capital and execution exposure: SQM's share of expansion capex is estimated at US$450-500 million, second-concentrator construction is expected to start in H2 2027, and first expansion volumes are expected in H1 2030.

The expansion is intended to double nameplate spodumene concentrate capacity from about 380,000 to 760,000 tonnes per year and lower unit operating costs; therefore the resilience thesis depends on scale benefits arriving without lithium-market absorption deteriorating before the 2030 ramp.

risks.risk: US$450-500 million of attributable expansion capex is committed years ahead of first expected expansion output, exposing returns to construction execution, commissioning timing and lithium-cycle conditions through 2030.
risks.falsifier: On-budget/on-schedule delivery plus sustained demand absorption and lower unit costs demonstrate resilient project economics through the ramp.

risks.risk: Doubling concentrate capacity can improve cost position but also increases volume exposed to commodity-price clearing if industry supply growth outruns battery demand.
risks.falsifier: Market demand absorbs incremental capacity while Mt Holland retains competitive unit economics and utilization.

unknowns.unknown: Realized project returns under normalized lithium prices and the final commissioning/ramp profile remain unverified by this source.

causalEdges.from: Mt Holland expansion capex and construction
causalEdges.to: future spodumene capacity and unit costs
causalEdges.mechanism: additional concentrator and ore sorting are intended to double nameplate output and improve scale economics
causalEdges.falsifier: cost overruns, commissioning delay, weak utilization or failure to lower unit costs

causalEdges.mechanism: commodity clearing prices determine how much value incremental capacity captures
causalEdges.falsifier: demand absorption sustains attractive economics despite new supply
